To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a functional role of the pretransmembrane segment of HIV-1 glycoprotein gp41 is the immersion of the sequence into lipid bilayers, which facilitates the oligomerization of this protein.
the pretransmembrane segment of HIV-1 envelope protein gp41 is functionally segmented and that this segmentation is important for the biological function of gp41.

The pretransmembrane segment connecting the helices from the carboxy-terminal (C) heptad repeat to the transmembrane (TM) anchor of HIV-1 envelope glycoprotein gp41 is functionally segmented in two consecutive subdomains.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the structure and function of the membrane-proximal gp41 pretransmemebrane segment, which is accessible to broadly reactive neutralizing antibodies and is a crucial component in the fusion process of the HIV-1 envelope protein gp160.
the role of the pretransmembrane segment of the gp41 envelope glycoprotein of human immunodeficient virus type 1.
understanding the molecular mechanisms of HIV-1 entry into cells, and with the development of novel anti-HIV-1 therapeutics and prophylactics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the gp41 membrane-proximal sequence is segmented in two consecutive subdomains.

1), gp41 pretransmemebrane segment is functionally segmented; 2), the N-terminal subdomain is amphipathic and extends helical bundle from the preceding heptad repeat; 3), the C-terminal subdomain is interfacial, and 4), the C-terminal hydrophobicity is crucial for gp41 function.

the gp41 pretrans-membrane segment, although not essential for fusion, is a key component of the viral membrane interface, where it may play a role in the fusion process and in the conformational changes of the fusion peptide.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the pretransmembrane segment of gp41 is segmented into two consecutive amphipathic and interfacial domains.
the pretransmembrane segment of the human immunodeficiency type virus gp41 is functionally segmented.

the membrane-proximal gp41 pretrans-membrane sequence (TM) plays a crucial role during fusion; it is accessible to broadly reactive neutralizing antibodies and it has a crucial role in the fusion activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have identified the membrane-proximal sequence of HIV-1 envelope glycoprotein (Env) gp41 as a functional unit.
the membrane-proximal region of gp41 is functionally segmented and that the C-terminal subdomain is the most important for membrane insertion, fusion inhibition and immunogenicity.
the gp41 pretrans-membrane region is segmented into two consecutive domains: one amphipatic and one fully inter-facial.
